name: Vanuatu

flag.description: Red over green horizontal halves with a black triangle at the hoist, separated by a yellow horizontal Y edged in black; the triangle holds a yellow curled boar's tusk around two crossed namele fern leaves.
flag.symbolism: Red stands for the blood of boars and people, green for the islands' richness and black for the Ni-Vanuatu people; the yellow Y traces the shape of the archipelago, the tusk symbolises prosperity and the namele leaves peace.

hook: A yellow sideways Y plus a curled boar's tusk in the black triangle: South Africa has a similar Y but no tusk, and adds blue.
trivia: Before independence in 1980 the islands were the New Hebrides, jointly ruled by Britain and France.
The land-diving ritual of Pentecost Island, leaping from tall towers with vines tied to the ankles, inspired modern bungee jumping.
